title: Minimum Vertex Cover
blocks: Minimum Vertex Cover
Problem Description

In a minimum vertex cover (MVC) problem, an undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\) in given. The goal is to select the smallest subset of nodes such that at least one end point of every edge in the graph is selected:: \[\min \sum_{v\in V} x_v \] \[\textrm{s.t.} x_u+x_v\geq 1, \,\forall (u,v)\in E, \] \[ x_v\in\{0,1\}, \, \forall v\in V.\] The graph \(G\) is typically a Erdos-Renyi or a Barabasi-Albert random graph.

Related literature
Large Neighborhood Search

For large neighborhood search, Huang et al. [Huang23] use Barabasi-Albert graphs with 1,000 and 2,000 nodes and affinity set to 70. The set of instances with 1000 nodes was used for training. The set of instances with 2000 nodes was used as an out-of-distribution test set. MVC has been used in [Song20, Huang23, Huang23b].  In addition to the distributions complied in Distributional MIPLIB shown in the table above, Song et al. [Song20] use both Erdos-Renyi and Barabasi-Albert graphs with 1,000 nodes and affinity set to 4.  Huang et al. [Huang23b] use Barabasi-Albert graphs with 9,000 nodes and affinity set to 5 to test a heuristic.
